subject: Onboarding acceptance: Neptune Retail load script, targets & results
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@neptuneretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding acceptance: initial load script + targets

Hi Tessa / Monica —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We want to lock the acceptance criteria so our SREs can run the test in our environment on Friday. High level asks:

- Confirm the throughput and latency targets we should validate against (p95/p99).
- Share a recommended load script (sequence lengths, token distribution) we can run in our staging environment.
- Let us know what evidence artifacts you need for sign-off.

I've attached our initial YAML (neptune-loadscript.yml) that models our peak-hour traffic. The script includes a mix of short chat-style prompts and longer product-summary generations — roughly 60/40.

Can you review and confirm the acceptance matrix and what counts as pass/fail? Dan (cc) will own the execution.

Appreciate it —
Anna
Senior Platform Engineer
Neptune Retail

Attachment: neptune-loadscript.yml (yaml, 12KB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@neptuneretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding acceptance: initial load script + targets

Thanks Anna — this looks good as a starting point. Quick readout of what we'll validate and how we'll share evidence. See inline high-level plan: 

1) Acceptance targets (pass conditions):
   - Throughput: sustain 480 QPS steady-state for 10 minutes with <= 2x CPU baseline variance.
   - Latency: p95 <= 220ms and p99 <= 520ms for text-generation routes at your avg sequence length (approx 75 tokens).
   - Error budget: total failed requests <= 0.5% during test window.

2) Test phases (we recommend running in this order):
   - Phase A (smoke): single-node 60s sanity run to ensure script compatibility.
   - Phase B (ramp): 5-min ramp to 50% target QPS, then 10-min hold at 100% (480 QPS).
   - Phase C (soak): 30-min soak at 70-100% depending on results to look for performance degradation and cache warmup effects.

3) Telemetry & artifacts to collect (what we need for sign-off):
   - Raw request/response traces (sampled at 1 in 100) + token counts per request.
   - Per-token cost summary and aggregate token volume.
   - Per-host CPU/GPU utilization and memory/kvcache hit-rate CSVs.
   - The full runner log and the generated results ZIP (neptune-results-20280316.zip).

4) Roles/responsibilities:
   - Neptune: run load using the attached YAML from your staging cluster; collect runner logs and upload results to the shared Drive link. Dan will execute.
   - Redwood (Monica + Karthik): we will review artifacts, run our independent validation against the same set of requests (where possible), and provide a pass/fail summary and remediation items if needed.

5) Timing suggestion:
   - Run tests Friday 2028-03-16 09:00-11:00 PT (Neptune executes).
   - Redwood will review artifacts and aim to provide findings by EOD 2028-03-16.

I've attached an acceptance matrix PDF (redwood-acceptance-matrix.pdf) that maps the pass criteria to evidence types. If you want to tweak targets (e.g., looser p99 during soak) let us know now so we can align scripts.

Cheers,
Tessa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-acceptance-matrix.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Dan Wu <dan.wu@neptuneretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>; Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding acceptance: initial load script + targets

Tessa / team —

We ran the planned phases this morning. Quick executive summary:

- Phase A/B completed cleanly. Phase C soak ran for 30m at ~72% sustained load (350 QPS).
- p95 observed: 190ms, p99 observed: 490ms. Error rate: 0.3% (mostly HTTP 429 from an upstream cache miss spike).
- Attached results bundle (neptune-results-20280316.zip) and runner logs. Host CPU peaked at 78%; GPU memory and kvcache warmed up as expected.

Questions for Redwood:
1) We saw a 12% token cost delta vs baseline when calls included longer summaries — is that expected for the model variant?
2) For the 429s during the soak, would you recommend increasing burst capacity or tuning the client-side retry backoff?

We've uploaded artifacts to the Drive link provided and copied the ZIP here as well. If these numbers meet the acceptance matrix, we'd like to move to production enablement next week.

Thanks,
Dan
SRE Lead, Neptune Retail

Attachments: neptune-results-20280316.zip (zip, 2.3MB)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Dan Wu <dan.wu@neptuneretail.com>; Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding acceptance: initial load script + targets

Thanks Dan — solid results and thanks for the thorough artifacts. Quick notes and next steps: 

- Acceptance decision: PASS with two minor follow-ups. p95/p99 are within the matrix and error budget is below threshold. Marking as accepted for the initial rollout.

- Follow-ups (owned):
  1) Retry/backoff tuning — Karthik will share a recommended backoff config and we suggest a short retest of the soak at 80% load to validate the 429 reduction. (Action: Karthik, target 2028-03-18)
  2) Token-cost variance — Laura will run a model-profile pass and provide a breakdown of per-request token encoding differences; we may recommend pinning a quantization variant to reduce cost delta. (Action: Laura, target 2028-03-20)

- Enablement: Once the two follow-ups are complete we'll schedule the production enablement window. For the immediate next step, can Neptune confirm a preferred date next week for a production flip (we recommend Tue 2028-03-21 02:00-04:00 PT)?

Thanks everyone — happy to call this out if you prefer a short sync to walk through the artifacts.

Best,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
